log.content:
This is a structural property check based on set theory and cardinalities. I will substitute the proposed form of $f(T)$ into the functional equation and verify the identity using properties of set intersections and unions.

The functional equation is:
$$f(T_1)f(T_2) = f(T_1 \cup T_2)f(T_1 \cap T_2)$$

We are given $f(T) = 2^{|T \cap I|}$ for a fixed set $I$.

Substituting this into the equation:
$$2^{|T_1 \cap I|} 2^{|T_2 \cap I|} = 2^{|(T_1 \cup T_2) \cap I|} 2^{|(T_1 \cap T_2) \cap I|}$$

Equating the exponents, we need to prove:
$$|T_1 \cap I| + |T_2 \cap I| = |(T_1 \cup T_2) \cap I| + |(T_1 \cap T_2) \cap I|$$

Let $A = T_1 \cap I$ and $B = T_2 \cap I$. Note that $A$ and $B$ are subsets of $I$.
We use the distributive laws of set operations:
$$(T_1 \cup T_2) \cap I = (T_1 \cap I) \cup (T_2 \cap I) = A \cup B$$
$$(T_1 \cap T_2) \cap I = (T_1 \cap I) \cap (T_2 \cap I) = A \cap B$$

The required identity simplifies to:
$$|A| + |B| = |A \cup B| + |A \cap B|$$

By the Inclusion-Exclusion Principle:
$$|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$$

Substituting this into the RHS of the required identity:
$$\text{RHS} = |A \cup B| + |A \cap B| = (|A| + |B| - |A \cap B|) + |A \cap B|$$
$$\text{RHS} = |A| + |B|$$

Since LHS $= |A| + |B|$, the identity holds.

I will write this proof into the shared notes.

(T1 U T2) intersect I = A U B
(T1 n T2) intersect I = A n B

The required identity is:

Substituting this into the RHS:
RHS = (|A| + |B| - |A n B|) + |A n B| = |A| + |B|.

Since LHS = |A| + |B|, the functional equation is satisfied.
